c.tagline: Cobblestones, Art Nouveau spires, and Baltic charm on the Daugava.

taxi.fareNote: Use licensed taxis (Red Cab, Panda Taxi) or book via Bolt app to avoid tourist overcharging at Old Town taxi stands.

emergency.note: 112 is the universal EU emergency number and reaches all services; English-speaking operators are generally available.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Old Town; stag-party nightlife scams — rip-off bars and taxis

hood_desc: Riga's cobblestoned medieval core packed with Gothic spires, cafes and the Freedom Monument, ideal for first-time visitors who want everything within walking distance.
Leafy boulevards lined with Europe's finest Art Nouveau facades and upscale boutiques, suited to architecture lovers and travelers wanting an elegant, quieter base close to downtown.

A leafy left-bank residential district with wooden houses, a historic covered market and a growing cafe scene, good for travelers wanting a local, less touristy feel with easy tram access to the center.
A bohemian strip of independent cafes, craft breweries and street art in the Avoti area, popular with younger travelers and creatives seeking Riga's hipster side.
The gritty, up-and-coming zone around the Zeppelin-hangar Central Market and train station, offering cheap eats and budget stays within walking distance of Old Town.
lodging: Riga Old Town Hostel & Backpackers Pub
Radisson Blu Hotel & Spa, Daugava Riga

water.note: Meets EU standards and is safe to drink; even ice in bars and restaurants is made from treated tap water.

transit.pay: Buy single tickets, day passes, or top up an e-talon smart card at kiosks, ticket machines, or the Rīgas satiksme app; contactless bank cards can now also be tapped directly on trams and buses. Tickets bought from the driver cost more than pre-purchased ones.
transit.hours: Most routes operate roughly 5:30am-11:30pm; a few night bus/tram lines run later on weekends.
transit.note: Validate or tap your ticket immediately after boarding; fare inspectors issue on-the-spot fines for invalid tickets.

train: Latvian Railways (Vivi) domestic and regional trains
International rail-bus combinations to Vilnius and Tallinn (Rail Baltica under construction)
bus: Rīgas satiksme city buses, trolleybuses and trams
Ecolines and Lux Express intercity/international coaches
ferry: Stena Line overnight ferry to Stockholm

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% in restaurants for good service is customary and appreciated.

landmarks: House of the Black Heads
Riga's most ornate and photographed building, a lavishly decorated Dutch Renaissance guildhall facade in Town Hall Square.
Freedom Monument
A soaring granite and copper monument topped by 'Liberty' holding three stars, the powerful symbol of Latvian independence.
Riga Cathedral (Dome Cathedral)
The largest medieval church in the Baltics, renowned for its massive organ and centuries-old architecture in Old Town.
St. Peter's Church
A soaring Gothic brick church whose tower offers the best panoramic views over Riga's red-roofed Old Town.
Riga Art Nouveau architecture (Alberta iela)
A street of extravagant, ornamented Art Nouveau facades that make Riga a world capital of the architectural style.
Three Brothers (Trīs brāļi)
A charming row of three medieval houses spanning centuries of styles, among the oldest stone buildings in Riga.
Riga Central Market
A UNESCO-listed market housed in giant former Zeppelin hangars, a vibrant and historic hub of local life.
Swedish Gate (Zviedru vārti)
The only surviving gate of Riga's old city walls, a quaint and atmospheric 17th-century passageway steeped in legend.
Riga TV Tower
A striking tripod-shaped tower and the tallest structure in the Baltic states, offering sweeping city and river views.
Town Hall Square and Old Town skyline
The historic heart of Riga, with its cluster of spires and gabled roofs forming the city's classic postcard view.

train.note: Trains leave from Riga Central Station, which is being rebuilt for Rail Baltica - allow extra time. Services to Russia and Belarus are suspended. The daily Vilnius-Riga-Valga train connects at Valga with an Estonian train to Tartu and Tallinn.

intl.to: Baltic states, Poland, Germany & Western Europe

bus.note: International coaches use Riga International Coach Terminal (Pragas iela 1), next to the Central Market. Buses are the main way between the Baltic capitals, running roughly hourly to Tallinn and Vilnius.

ferry.note: The Riga-Stockholm ferry has been suspended since 2020 and had still not resumed as of mid-2026. The nearest international ferries sail with Stena Line from Liepaja to Travemunde (Germany) and from Ventspils to Nynashamn (Sweden) - see https://www.stenalinetravel.com/.

half.name: Jurmala
half.blurb: Breezy Baltic resort town famed for sandy beaches, pine forests, and charming wooden art nouveau villas.

half.name: Sigulda
half.blurb: Green hilly town nicknamed Latvian Switzerland, dotted with medieval castles, caves, and forested river valleys.

half.name: Cesis
half.blurb: Enchanting medieval town built around a dramatic castle, with cobbled lanes and leafy old streets.

half.name: Kemeri National Park
half.blurb: Wild wetland reserve where a boardwalk trail winds across a hauntingly beautiful raised peat bog.

half.name: Rundale Palace
half.blurb: Opulent baroque palace with lavish gilded rooms and formal French gardens, often called Latvia's Versailles.

half.name: Kuldiga
half.blurb: Picturesque riverside town home to Europe's widest waterfall and a photogenic old brick bridge.
